newsitem.title: IRAQ: Turkish troops on anti-rebel assault in Iraq.
newsitem.headline: Turkish troops on anti-rebel assault in Iraq.

text.p: Several thousand Turkish troops, backed by tanks and heavy artillery, pushed across the border into northern Iraq early on Wednesday in a move against separatist Kurdish rebel bases.

Witnesses said the assault, which began at 3 a.m. (2300 GMT) followed a security sweep by local Iraqi Kurdish authorities, who ordered all journalists to leave the border region, confiscated mobile telephones and film.

"Three thousand troops, including tanks and artillery, started crossing at 2300 GMT and they are still continuing," a resident close to the border said. Other witnesses said troops later headed northeast away from Zakho.

The state-run Anatolian news agency reported clashes between troops and the Turkish separatist Kurdistan Workers Party (PKK), in a region it identified as Sarisarilar. It also said troops had cornered a group of PKK just inside the Iraqi border opposite Turkey's eastern border region of Hakkari.
The agency said Turkish forces supported by Cobra helicopters had inflicted heavy losses on the PKK.
Baghdad protested against the move, saying it contravened international law. It said there had been many casualties.

"The government of the Republic of Iraq vehemently condemns this new Turkish military aggression on the sovereignty of Iraq and its territorial integrity," the Iraqi news agency INA said, quoting a Foreign Ministry spokesman.
The spokesman said the Iraqi government "calls on the Turkish government to withdraw its invading troops from inside Iraqi territory immediately".
A Turkish Foreign Ministry spokesman said the operation was a "limited" one, in coordination with local Iraqi Kurds, to oust PKK guerrillas from the border marshes.

However, a senior security source told Reuters: "This is a wide and comprehensive operation." The border areas of northern Iraq have in the past been the scene of firefights between Turkish security forces and PKK guerrillas.
Turkish army officers inside Iraq were tight-lipped, one saying only: "We are here on exercises."
Residents on the Turkish side said the border crossing at Habur was closed to all civilian traffic.
"There is a news blackout. No member of the press is permitted access to Zakho," a local Iraqi Kurdish official said.
Turkish soldiers later enforced the news blackout, barring reporters from returning to the area.
The Iraqi side of the border is under the general control of Massoud Barzani's KDP, a rival of the separatist PKK fighting for independence or autonomy in southeast Turkey.
An Iraqi opposition source told Reuters that the KDP had been fighting the PKK since Monday.
Northern Iraq was set up as an Western-backed autonomous Kurdish area following the 1991 Gulf War. The KDP and another Kurdish group have shared power, if acrimoniously, since then.
Barzani teamed up last year with forces of Iraqi President Saddam Hussein against rival Iraqi Kurdish leader Jalal Talabani, prompting U.S. missile strikes against Iraqi targets.

Turkish troops regularly cross back and forth in "hot pursuit" of the PKK. In March 1995, tens of thousands of troops pushed deep into Iraq for a prolonged campaign that drove the PKK back but failed to crush them.

A KDP representative in the southeastern Turkish city of Diyarbakir said Turkish jets flew bombing missions from a base there. Turkish jets recently stepped up cross-border bombings into northern Iraq, according to reports from the region.
Troops were also fighting the PKK within Turkey's borders. Security officials said troops had killed 30 Kurdish rebels in clashes in the southeast in the last two days.
More than 22,000 people have been killed in more than 12 years of fighting between the army and the PKK, which is seeking autonomy or independence in mainly Kurdish southeastern Turkey.
